sources.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.abstract: Large policies pretrained on a combination of Internet-scale vision-language data and diverse robot demonstrations have the potential to change how we teach robots new skills: rather than training new behaviors from scratch, we can fine-tune such vision-language-action (VLA) models to obtain robust, generalizable policies for visuomotor control. Yet, widespread adoption of VLAs for robotics has been challenging as 1) existing VLAs are largely closed and inaccessible to the public, and 2) prior work fails to explore methods for efficiently fine-tuning VLAs for new tasks, a key component for adoption. Addressing these challenges, we introduce OpenVLA, a 7B-parameter open-source VLA trained on a diverse collection of 970k real-world robot demonstrations. OpenVLA builds on a Llama 2 language model combined with a visual encoder that fuses pretrained features from DINOv2 and SigLIP. As a product of the added data diversity and new model components, OpenVLA demonstrates strong results for generalist manipulation, outperforming closed models such as RT-2-X (55B) by 16.5% in absolute task success rate across 29 tasks and multiple robot embodiments, with 7x fewer parameters. We further show that we can effectively fine-tune OpenVLA for new settings, with especially strong generalization results in multi-task environments involving multiple objects and strong language grounding abilities, and outperform expressive from-scratch imitation learning methods such as Diffusion Policy by 20.4%. We also explore compute efficiency; as a separate contribution, we show that OpenVLA can be fine-tuned on consumer GPUs via modern low-rank adaptation methods and served efficiently via quantization without a hit to downstream success rate. Finally, we release model checkpoints, fine-tuning notebooks, and our PyTorch codebase with built-in support for training VLAs at scale on Open X-Embodiment datasets.

sources.title: Unified Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) have garnered significant attention for their potential in advancing robotic manipulation. However, previous approaches predominantly rely on the general comprehension capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to generate action signals, often overlooking the rich temporal and causal structure embedded in visual observations. In this paper, we present UniVLA, a unified and native multimodal VLA model that autoregressively models vision, language, and action signals as discrete token sequences. This formulation enables flexible multimodal tasks learning, particularly from large-scale video data. By incorporating world modeling during post-training, UniVLA captures causal dynamics from videos, facilitating effective transfer to downstream policy learning--especially for long-horizon tasks. Our approach sets new state-of-the-art results across several widely used simulation benchmarks, including CALVIN, LIBERO, and Simplenv-Bridge, significantly surpassing previous methods. For example, UniVLA achieves 95.5% average success rate on LIBERO benchmark, surpassing pi0-FAST's 85.5%. We further demonstrate its broad applicability on real-world ALOHA manipulation and autonomous driving.

sources.title: Explainable Adversarial-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
sources.abstract: Smart farming has emerged as a key technology for advancing modern agriculture through automation and intelligent control. However, systems relying on RGB cameras for perception and robotic manipulators for control, common in smart farming, are vulnerable to photometric perturbations such as hue, illumination, and noise changes, which can cause malfunction under adversarial attacks. To address this issue, we propose an explainable adversarial-robust Vision-Language-Action model based on the OpenVLA-OFT framework. The model integrates an Evidence-3 module that detects photometric perturbations and generates natural language explanations of their causes and effects. Experiments show that the proposed model reduces Current Action L1 loss by 21.7% and Next Actions L1 loss by 18.4% compared to the baseline, demonstrating improved action prediction accuracy and explainability under adversarial conditions.

sources.title: FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.abstract: Autoregressivesequence models, such as Transformer-based vision-language action (VLA) policies, can be tremendously effective for capturing complex and generalizable robotic behaviors.However, such models require us to choose a tokenization of our continuous action signals, which determines how the discrete symbols predicted by the model map to continuous robot actions.We find that current approaches for robot action tokenization, based on simple per-dimension, per-timestep binning schemes, typically perform poorly when learning dexterous skills from high-frequency robot data.To address this challenge, we propose a new compression-based tokenization scheme for robot actions, based on the discrete cosine transform.Our tokenization approach, Frequency-space Action Sequence Tokenization (FAST), enables us to train autoregressive VLAs for highly dexterous and high-frequency tasks where standard discretization methods fail completely.Based on FAST, we release FAST+, a universal robot action tokenizer, trained on 1M real robot action trajectories.It can be used as a black-box tokenizer for a wide range of robot action sequences, with diverse action spaces and control frequencies.Finally, we show that, when combined with the π0 VLA, our method can scale to training on 10k hours of robot data and match the performance of diffusion VLAs, while reducing training time by up to 5x.

sources.title: ShowUI: One Vision-Language-Action Model for GUI Visual Agent
sources.abstract: Building Graphical User Interface (GUI) assistants holds significant promise for enhancing human workflow productivity. While most agents are language-based, relying on closed-source API with text-rich meta-information (e.g., HTML or accessibility tree), they show limitations in perceiving UI visuals as humans do, highlighting the need for GUI visual agents. In this work, we develop a vision-language-action model in digital world, namely ShowUI, which features the following innovations: (i) UI-Guided Visual Token Selection to reduce computational costs by formulating screenshots as an UI connected graph, adaptively identifying their redundant relationship and serve as the criteria for token selection during self-attention blocks; (ii) Interleaved Vision-Language-Action Streaming that flexibly unifies diverse needs within GUI tasks, enabling effective management of visual-action history in navigation or pairing multi-turn query-action sequences per screenshot to enhance training efficiency; (iii) Small-scale High-quality GUI Instruction-following Datasets by careful data curation and employing a resampling strategy to address significant data type imbalances. With above components, ShowUI, a lightweight 2B model using 256K data, achieves a strong 75.1% accuracy in zero-shot screenshot grounding. Its UI-guided token selection further reduces 33% of redundant visual tokens during training and speeds up the performance by 1.4x. Navigation experiments across web Mind2Web, mobile AITW, and online MiniWob environments further underscore the effectiveness and potential of our model in advancing GUI visual agents. The models are available at https://github.com/showlab/ShowUI.

sources.title: A Survey on Vision--Language--Action Models for Embodied AI
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
sources.abstract: Embodied AI is widely recognized as a cornerstone of artificial general intelligence (AGI) because it involves controlling embodied agents to perform tasks in the physical world. Building on the success of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), a new category of multimodal models-referred to as vision-language-action (VLA) models-has emerged to address language-conditioned robotic tasks in embodied AI by leveraging their distinct ability to generate actions. The recent proliferation of VLAs necessitates a comprehensive survey to capture the rapidly evolving landscape. To this end, we present the first survey on VLAs for embodied AI. This work provides a detailed taxonomy of VLAs, organized into three major lines of research. The first line focuses on individual components of VLAs. The second line is dedicated to developing VLA-based control policies adept at predicting low-level actions. The third line comprises high-level task planners capable of decomposing long-horizon tasks into a sequence of subtasks, thereby guiding VLAs to follow more general user instructions. Furthermore, we provide an extensive summary of relevant resources, including datasets, simulators, and benchmarks. Finally, we discuss the challenges facing VLAs and outline promising future directions in embodied AI. A curated repository associated with this survey is available at: https://github.com/yueen-ma/Awesome-VLA.

sources.title: Vlaser: Vision-Language-Action Model with Synergistic Embodied Reasoning
sources.abstract: While significant research has focused on developing embodied reasoning capabilities using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) or integrating advanced VLMs into Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for end-to-end robot control, few studies directly address the critical gap between upstream VLM-based reasoning and downstream VLA policy learning. In this work, we take an initial step toward bridging embodied reasoning with VLA policy learning by introducing Vlaser - a Vision-Language-Action Model with synergistic embodied reasoning capability, which is a foundational vision-language model designed to integrate high-level reasoning with low-level control for embodied agents. Built upon the high-quality Vlaser-6M dataset, Vlaser achieves state-of-the-art performance across a range of embodied reasoning benchmarks - including spatial reasoning, embodied grounding, embodied QA, and task planning. Furthermore, we systematically examine how different VLM initializations affect supervised VLA fine-tuning, offering novel insights into mitigating the domain shift between internet-scale pre-training data and embodied-specific policy learning data. Based on these insights, our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on the WidowX benchmark and competitive performance on the Google Robot benchmark.

sources.title: SmolVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Affordable and Efficient Robotics
sources.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) pretrained on large-scale multimodal datasets encode rich visual and linguistic knowledge, making them a strong foundation for robotics. Rather than training robotic policies from scratch, recent approaches adapt VLMs into vision-language-action (VLA) models that enable natural language-driven perception and control. However, existing VLAs are typically massive--often with billions of parameters--leading to high training costs and limited real-world deployability. Moreover, they rely on academic and industrial datasets, overlooking the growing availability of community-collected data from affordable robotic platforms. In this work, we present SmolVLA, a small, efficient, and community-driven VLA that drastically reduces both training and inference costs, while retaining competitive performance. SmolVLA is designed to be trained on a single GPU and deployed on consumer-grade GPUs or even CPUs. To further improve responsiveness, we introduce an asynchronous inference stack decoupling perception and action prediction from action execution, allowing higher control rates with chunked action generation. Despite its compact size, SmolVLA achieves performance comparable to VLAs that are 10x larger. We evaluate SmolVLA on a range of both simulated as well as real-world robotic benchmarks and release all code, pretrained models, and training data.

sources.title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
sources.abstract: This paper proposes to solve the problem of Vision-and-Language Navigation with legged robots, which not only provides a flexible way for humans to command but also allows the robot to navigate through more challenging and cluttered scenes. However, it is non-trivial to translate human language instructions all the way to low-level leg joint actions. We propose NaVILA, a 2-level framework that unifies a Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) with locomotion skills. Instead of directly predicting low-level actions from VLA, NaVILA first generates mid-level actions with spatial information in the form of language, (e.g., "moving forward 75cm"), which serves as an input for a visual locomotion RL policy for execution. NaVILA substantially improves previous approaches on existing benchmarks. The same advantages are demonstrated in our newly developed benchmarks with IsaacLab, featuring more realistic scenes, low-level controls, and real-world robot experiments. We show more results at https://navila-bot.github.io/

sources.title: $π_{0.5}$: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.abstract: In order for robots to be useful, they must perform practically relevant tasks in the real world, outside of the lab. While vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated impressive results for end-to-end robot control, it remains an open question how far such models can generalize in the wild. We describe $π_{0.5}$, a new model based on $π_{0}$ that uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks to enable broad generalization. $π_{0.5}$\ uses data from multiple robots, high-level semantic prediction, web data, and other sources to enable broadly generalizable real-world robotic manipulation. Our system uses a combination of co-training and hybrid multi-modal examples that combine image observations, language commands, object detections, semantic subtask prediction, and low-level actions. Our experiments show that this kind of knowledge transfer is essential for effective generalization, and we demonstrate for the first time that an end-to-end learning-enabled robotic system can perform long-horizon and dexterous manipulation skills, such as cleaning a kitchen or bedroom, in entirely new homes.

sources.title: GesVLA: Gesture-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model Embedded Representations
sources.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robot manipulation by unifying perception and action. However, existing VLA systems primarily rely on textual instructions and struggle to resolve spatial ambiguity in complex scenes with multiple similar objects. To address this limitation, we introduce gesture as a parallel instruction modality and propose a Gesture-aware Vision-Language-Action model (GesVLA). Our approach encodes gesture features directly into the latent space, enabling them to participate in both high-level reasoning and low-level action generation, and adopts a dual-VLM architecture to achieve tight coupling between gesture representations and action policies. At the data level, we construct a scalable gesture data generation pipeline by rendering hand models onto real-world scene images. This reduces the sim-to-real visual gap while producing rich data with diverse motion patterns and corresponding pointing annotations. In addition, we employ a two-stage training strategy to equip the model with both gesture perception and action prediction capabilities. We evaluate our approach on multiple real-world robotic tasks, including a controlled block manipulation task for validation and more practical scenarios such as product and produce selection. Experimental results show that incorporating gesture consistently improves target grounding accuracy and human-robot interaction efficiency, especially in complex and cluttered environments. Project page: https://gwxuan.github.io/GesVLA/.

sources.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
sources.abstract: We study how vision-language models trained on Internet-scale data can be incorporated directly into end-to-end robotic control to boost generalization and enable emergent semantic reasoning. Our goal is to enable a single end-to-end trained model to both learn to map robot observations to actions and enjoy the benefits of large-scale pretraining on language and vision-language data from the web. To this end, we propose to co-fine-tune state-of-the-art vision-language models on both robotic trajectory data and Internet-scale vision-language tasks, such as visual question answering. In contrast to other approaches, we propose a simple, general recipe to achieve this goal: in order to fit both natural language responses and robotic actions into the same format, we express the actions as text tokens and incorporate them directly into the training set of the model in the same way as natural language tokens. We refer to such category of models as vision-language-action models (VLA) and instantiate an example of such a model, which we call RT-2. Our extensive evaluation (6k evaluation trials) shows that our approach leads to performant robotic policies and enables RT-2 to obtain a range of emergent capabilities from Internet-scale training. This includes significantly improved generalization to novel objects, the ability to interpret commands not present in the robot training data (such as placing an object onto a particular number or icon), and the ability to perform rudimentary reasoning in response to user commands (such as picking up the smallest or largest object, or the one closest to another object). We further show that incorporating chain of thought reasoning allows RT-2 to perform multi-stage semantic reasoning, for example figuring out which object to pick up for use as an improvised hammer (a rock), or which type of drink is best suited for someone who is tired (an energy drink).

sources.title: A Survey on Vision-Language-Action Models: An Action Tokenization Perspective
sources.abstract: The remarkable advancements of vision and language foundation models in multimodal understanding, reasoning, and generation has sparked growing efforts to extend such intelligence to the physical world, fueling the flourishing of vision-language-action (VLA) models. Despite seemingly diverse approaches, we observe that current VLA models can be unified under a single framework: vision and language inputs are processed by a series of VLA modules, producing a chain of \textit{action tokens} that progressively encode more grounded and actionable information, ultimately generating executable actions. We further determine that the primary design choice distinguishing VLA models lies in how action tokens are formulated, which can be categorized into language description, code, affordance, trajectory, goal state, latent representation, raw action, and reasoning. However, there remains a lack of comprehensive understanding regarding action tokens, significantly impeding effective VLA development and obscuring future directions. Therefore, this survey aims to categorize and interpret existing VLA research through the lens of action tokenization, distill the strengths and limitations of each token type, and identify areas for improvement. Through this systematic review and analysis, we offer a synthesized outlook on the broader evolution of VLA models, highlight underexplored yet promising directions, and contribute guidance for future research, hoping to bring the field closer to general-purpose intelligence.

sources.title: DreamVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Dreamed with Comprehensive World Knowledge
sources.abstract: Recent advances in vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise in integrating image generation with action prediction to improve generalization and reasoning in robot manipulation. However, existing methods are limited to challenging image-based forecasting, which suffers from redundant information and lacks comprehensive and critical world knowledge, including dynamic, spatial and semantic information. To address these limitations, we propose DreamVLA, a novel VLA framework that integrates comprehensive world knowledge forecasting to enable inverse dynamics modeling, thereby establishing a perception-prediction-action loop for manipulation tasks. Specifically, DreamVLA introduces a dynamic-region-guided world knowledge prediction, integrated with the spatial and semantic cues, which provide compact yet comprehensive representations for action planning. This design aligns with how humans interact with the world by first forming abstract multimodal reasoning chains before acting. To mitigate interference among the dynamic, spatial and semantic information during training, we adopt a block-wise structured attention mechanism that masks their mutual attention, preventing information leakage and keeping each representation clean and disentangled. Moreover, to model the conditional distribution over future actions, we employ a diffusion-based transformer that disentangles action representations from shared latent features. Extensive experiments on both real-world and simulation environments demonstrate that DreamVLA achieves 76.7% success rate on real robot tasks and 4.44 average length on the CALVIN ABC-D benchmarks.

sources.title: StereoVLA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Models with Stereo Vision
sources.abstract: While Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel in generalist manipulation, they often lack fine-grained spatial awareness and show limited viewpoint robustness. This limitation largely stems from the reliance on pretrained RGB encoders, which lack explicit geometric cues and prioritize semantic alignment over geometric representation. We argue that effective visual representations for VLA models must jointly encode both semantic and geometric information. In this paper, we introduce StereoVLA, the first VLA model to incorporate rich geometric cues from large-scale synthetic stereo data. StereoVLA employs a Geometric-and-Semantic (GeoSem) vision encoder that extracts geometric cues from subtle stereo-view disparities for precise spatial perception, while simultaneously capturing semantic features from pixel observations to support language-conditioned manipulation. Additionally, we introduce two synergistic co-training objectives: Interaction-Region Depth Estimation for precise spatial reasoning, and Camera Parameter Estimation to implicitly align perception and action coordinate systems. Compared with baselines that employ various input modalities, StereoVLA achieves a 33.4% absolute gain in success rate in real-world experiments and demonstrates robustness to near-hemispheric camera perspectives. Project page: https://shengliangd.github.io/StereoVLA-Webpage.

sources.title: VLM4VLA: Revisiting Vision-Language-Models in Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, which integrate pretrained large Vision-Language Models (VLM) into their policy backbone, are gaining significant attention for their promising generalization capabilities. This paper revisits a fundamental yet seldom systematically studied question: how VLM choice and competence translate to downstream VLA policies performance? We introduce VLM4VLA, a minimal adaptation pipeline that converts general-purpose VLMs into VLA policies using only a small set of new learnable parameters for fair and efficient comparison. Despite its simplicity, VLM4VLA proves surprisingly competitive with more sophisticated network designs. Through extensive empirical studies on various downstream tasks across three benchmarks, we find that while VLM initialization offers a consistent benefit over training from scratch, a VLM's general capabilities are poor predictors of its downstream task performance. This challenges common assumptions, indicating that standard VLM competence is necessary but insufficient for effective embodied control. We further investigate the impact of specific embodied capabilities by fine-tuning VLMs on seven auxiliary embodied tasks (e.g., embodied QA, visual pointing, depth estimation). Contrary to intuition, improving a VLM's performance on specific embodied skills does not guarantee better downstream control performance. Finally, modality-level ablations identify the visual module in VLM, rather than the language component, as the primary performance bottleneck. We demonstrate that injecting control-relevant supervision into the vision encoder of the VLM yields consistent gains, even when the encoder remains frozen during downstream fine-tuning. This isolates a persistent domain gap between current VLM pretraining objectives and the requirements of embodied action-planning.

sources.title: CogACT: A Foundational Vision-Language-Action Model for Synergizing Cognition and Action in Robotic Manipulation
sources.abstract: The advancement of large Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models has significantly improved robotic manipulation in terms of language-guided task execution and generalization to unseen scenarios. While existing VLAs adapted from pretrained large Vision-Language-Models (VLM) have demonstrated promising generalizability, their task performance is still unsatisfactory as indicated by the low tasks success rates in different environments. In this paper, we present a new advanced VLA architecture derived from VLM. Unlike previous works that directly repurpose VLM for action prediction by simple action quantization, we propose a omponentized VLA architecture that has a specialized action module conditioned on VLM output. We systematically study the design of the action module and demonstrates the strong performance enhancement with diffusion action transformers for action sequence modeling, as well as their favorable scaling behaviors. We also conduct comprehensive experiments and ablation studies to evaluate the efficacy of our models with varied designs. The evaluation on 5 robot embodiments in simulation and real work shows that our model not only significantly surpasses existing VLAs in task performance and but also exhibits remarkable adaptation to new robots and generalization to unseen objects and backgrounds. It exceeds the average success rates of OpenVLA which has similar model size (7B) with ours by over 35% in simulated evaluation and 55% in real robot experiments. It also outperforms the large RT-2-X model (55B) by 18% absolute success rates in simulation. Code and models can be found on our project page (https://cogact.github.io/).

sources.title: Survey on Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.abstract: This paper presents an AI-generated review of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, summarizing key methodologies, findings, and future directions. The content is produced using large language models (LLMs) and is intended only for demonstration purposes. This work does not represent original research, but highlights how AI can help automate literature reviews. As AI-generated content becomes more prevalent, ensuring accuracy, reliability, and proper synthesis remains a challenge. Future research will focus on developing a structured framework for AI-assisted literature reviews, exploring techniques to enhance citation accuracy, source credibility, and contextual understanding. By examining the potential and limitations of LLM in academic writing, this study aims to contribute to the broader discussion of integrating AI into research workflows. This work serves as a preliminary step toward establishing systematic approaches for leveraging AI in literature review generation, making academic knowledge synthesis more efficient and scalable.

sources.title: Interactive Post-Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
sources.abstract: We introduce RIPT-VLA, a simple and scalable reinforcement-learning-based interactive post-training paradigm that fine-tunes pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models using only sparse binary success rewards. Existing VLA training pipelines rely heavily on offline expert demonstration data and supervised imitation, limiting their ability to adapt to new tasks and environments under low-data regimes. RIPT-VLA addresses this by enabling interactive post-training with a stable policy optimization algorithm based on dynamic rollout sampling and leave-one-out advantage estimation. RIPT-VLA has the following characteristics. First, it applies to various VLA models, resulting in an improvement on the lightweight QueST model by 21.2%, and the 7B OpenVLA-OFT model to an unprecedented 97.5% success rate. Second, it is computationally efficient and data-efficient: with only one demonstration, RIPT-VLA enables an unworkable SFT model (4%) to succeed with a 97% success rate within 15 iterations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the policy learned by RIPT-VLA generalizes across different tasks and scenarios and is robust to the initial state context. These results highlight RIPT-VLA as a practical and effective paradigm for post-training VLA models through minimal supervision.

sources.title: Dream-VL & Dream-VLA: Open Vision-Language and Vision-Language-Action Models with Diffusion Language Model Backbone
sources.abstract: While autoregressive Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable success, their sequential generation often limits their efficacy in complex visual planning and dynamic robotic control. In this work, we investigate the potential of constructing Vision-Language Models upon diffusion-based large language models (dLLMs) to overcome these limitations. We introduce Dream-VL, an open diffusion-based VLM (dVLM) that achieves state-of-the-art performance among previous dVLMs. Dream-VL is comparable to top-tier AR-based VLMs trained on open data on various benchmarks but exhibits superior potential when applied to visual planning tasks. Building upon Dream-VL, we introduce Dream-VLA, a dLLM-based Vision-Language-Action model (dVLA) developed through continuous pre-training on open robotic datasets. We demonstrate that the natively bidirectional nature of this diffusion backbone serves as a superior foundation for VLA tasks, inherently suited for action chunking and parallel generation, leading to significantly faster convergence in downstream fine-tuning. Dream-VLA achieves top-tier performance of 97.2% average success rate on LIBERO, 71.4% overall average on SimplerEnv-Bridge, and 60.5% overall average on SimplerEnv-Fractal, surpassing leading models such as $π_0$ and GR00T-N1. We also validate that dVLMs surpass AR baselines on downstream tasks across different training objectives. We release both Dream-VL and Dream-VLA to facilitate further research in the community.

market.coverage_note: Companies are chosen from the evidence: SEC-listed patent assignees and employers of paper authors found by the Patent and Science agents (24 company name(s) in the patents and papers; 0 matched to the SEC ticker file; the top 0 by patents + papers are read), plus filers whose reports mention the topic. Company evidence is limited to short verbatim passages from their latest SEC annual/quarterly reports that mention the keywords. 8-K press releases (exhibit files) are not read, and companies that do not file with the SEC (e.g. SK hynix, Samsung) are not covered. News items are headlines only: the articles were not read. Company size and trend figures (revenue, growth, R&D, net income) come from the SEC's XBRL company-facts data as reported by each company; the size class is by revenue, not market value. Companies marked 'discovered' were found by a full-text search of all SEC filings for the topic phrase only; no patent or paper of theirs was found, they are often small, and a mention in a filing says nothing about their size, role or prospects.

sources.title: Non-contact tomato picking control method based on vision-language-action model and control system thereof [CN122645293A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a non-contact tomato picking control method based on a vision-language-action model and a control system thereof, and the method comprises the following steps: collecting an RGB-D image and a natural language instruction, and respectively extracting vision and semantic features through ViT-Marge and T5-Marge; detecting key points of fruits and calyxes by using Center Net, and recovering three-dimensional picking points and directions in combination with a depth map; with the language features as queries and the visual features as key values, fusing ontology perception information through cross attention, and constructing state vectors; outputting an action instruction by adopting a multi-layer perceptron strategy network; and designing a reward function containing high-weight collision penalty, and combining behavior cloning and PPO two-stage training. According to the method, understanding of a natural language instruction is accurately close to collision-free, the collision rate of branches and leaves is remarkably reduced, and the picking success rate and the sim < 2 > real migration efficiency are improved.

sources.title: Self-adaptive step length control method for live broadcast interaction robot [CN122661480A]
authors: CHONGQING CHETU SHIJIE NETWORK TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: CHONGQING CHETU SHIJIE NETWORK TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of intelligent robot control, and particularly relates to a self-adaptive step length control method for a live broadcast interaction robot. Comprising the following steps: identifying a robot control instruction from bullet screen text information, and inputting the robot control instruction and a live scene image into a vision-language-action model for processing to obtain a candidate action sequence under current iteration; sequentially calculating window action deviation and convergence slope of each action site in the candidate action sequence; if the window action deviation and convergence slope of the first m action sites meet the stable condition, and the (m + 1) th action site does not meet the stable condition, outputting the first m action sites; otherwise, outputting the candidate action sequence again; the live broadcast interaction robot executes the first m action sites and continues to process the remaining action sites in the candidate action sequence at the same time until the whole robot control instruction is executed; according to the method, high-frequency low-delay interaction can be realized while the control stability is ensured, and the method is more suitable for a cost-sensitive and high-concurrency live broadcast environment.

sources.title: Vision-language-action model training method and device, model and application system [CN122637135A]
authors: BEIJING XINGDONG JIYUAN TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING XINGDONG JIYUAN TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vision-language-action model training method and device, a model and an application system, and the method comprises the steps: obtaining a real machine interaction data set facing a target business scene through a preset progressive closed-loop data collection process; wherein the progressive closed-loop data acquisition process comprises a basic acquisition stage, a directional acquisition stage, an error correction acquisition stage and an online acquisition stage; based on the real machine interaction data set, in combination with differentiated instructions designed for scene features, operation logic and task types, the vision-language-action model is trained, so that the vision-language-action model obtained through training has the cross-scene and cross-task generalization migration ability; and obtaining a vision-language-action model suitable for the target business scene.

sources.title: Dynamic memory enhancement method and system oriented to vision-language-action model, and readable storage medium [CN122634497A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a dynamic memory enhancement method and system oriented to a vision-language-action model, and a storage medium, and solves the problems of memory short vision, memory pollution and incapability of dynamically adjusting a fusion weight in a long-sight-distance task of an existing VLA model. The method comprises the following steps: constructing a working memory and retrieving a historical memory from a perception-cognition-reward memory library; performing adaptive weighted fusion on the current memory and the historical memory by using a gating network with trainable parameters to generate enhanced working memory; calculating a task progress difference value based on the enhanced working memory by adopting a progress evaluator, and generating a single-step intensive reward; performing online strategy optimization on gating network parameters by taking the reward as a dominant function; when the memory bank is full, reward weighted combination is carried out on adjacent entries based on weighted indexes of feature similarity and reward similarity; and finally, the action expert network outputs an action sequence. The method can be used for robot long-time-sequence task learning and adaptive control in a dynamic environment.

sources.title: Vision-language-action model-oriented look-ahead and review collaborative decision-making method and system [CN122615122A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a look-ahead and review collaborative decision-making method and system for a vision-language-action model, and the method comprises the steps: constructing a vision-language-action basic model, introducing a scene memory module, coding a current observation and instruction into a working memory, and retrieving historical context features from an external memory library through a cross attention mechanism; a generative world model is introduced, prospective lexical elements are added in model input, and future observation features are predicted with historical context features obtained through work memory and retrieval as conditions; a prediction deviation driven gating mechanism is introduced, deviation signals of prediction observation and real observation are evaluated, an adaptive gating value is calculated to dynamically fuse current observation and historical memory features, and fused context features, predicted future states and action query lexical elements are jointly input into an action decoder to generate control actions. According to the method, the problems of time sequence short view and error accumulation caused by the fact that an existing VLA model excessively depends on current single observation are effectively solved.

sources.title: Body robot action generation method, system and equipment based on structured action characterization and medium [CN122606657A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to a structured action representation-based motion generation method, system and equipment for a robot with a body, and a storage medium. The method comprises the following steps: inputting current observation information obtained by observing a current scene into a vision-language-action model based on an OneModel architecture, and extracting to obtain a potential strategy feature containing scene perception information and a task execution intention; determining a local coordinate system based on the potential strategy features; on the basis of the potential strategy features and a shared prototype action library, generating a local execution action corresponding to the current moment in a local coordinate system; converting the local execution action into an initial execution action in a world coordinate system; and based on the initial execution action and the supplementary control parameters, the final execution action of the robot with the body at the current moment is determined. Therefore, the cooperation between the task execution intention and the structured action representation can be realized by utilizing the OneModel architecture, and the action generation stability and generalization ability of the robot with the body are improved.

sources.title: Bolt tightening method based on vision-language-action model [CN122584293A]
authors: SHENYANG INTELLIGENT ROBOT INNOVATION CENTER CO LTD
sources.organization: SHENYANG INST AUTOMATION CAS, SHENYANG INTELLIGENT ROBOT INNOVATION CENTER CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a bolt tightening method based on a vision-language-action model, and belongs to the technical field of intelligent manufacturing. The method comprises the following steps: collecting scene image data of a target bolt and a peripheral workpiece area of the target bolt, and extracting multi-scale visual features from the collected scene image data to obtain a multi-scale visual feature vector Fv; performing semantic analysis on the natural language instruction to obtain a language feature vector F1; performing cross-modal feature alignment on the Fv and the Fl to obtain an aligned feature vector Fvl; performing action decoding and parameterized mapping processing on the Fvl to generate an action parameter vector Fd; and the Fd is input into a control execution module, kinematics solution and control instruction generation are carried out, and therefore automatic execution equipment is driven to complete bolt tightening operation. According to the method, the accuracy, adaptability and stability of bolt tightening work under complex working conditions can be improved, and the labor cost of bolt tightening work is effectively reduced.

sources.title: Robot control method based on lightweight multi-modal large model [CN122584370A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a robot control method based on a lightweight multi-modal large model, and relates to the technical field of body intelligence, robot control and multi-modal large models. In order to solve the problems that an existing vision-language-action model is low in calculation efficiency, high in training resource requirement and large in data dependence degree in actual deployment, a sparse activation control sub-module is constructed, and a part of network layers or attention branches in a pre-training multi-mode backbone network are selectively started; and a time sequence motion decoding module is constructed to fuse the current multi-mode hidden layer features and the historical time sequence context features so as to generate a robot motion instruction. According to the invention, a two-stage training method of offline feature extraction and action strategy learning decoupling is also adopted, multi-modal hidden layer features are cached, and a time sequence action decoding module is trained based on the cache, so that repeated trunk forward calculation and gradient return are reduced.

sources.title: Multi-modal robot long-range operation method based on large language model and symbol planning verification [CN122539345A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a multi-modal robot long-range operation method based on a large language model and symbol planning verification, and relates to the technical field of robot intelligent control, task planning and body intelligence. The method is oriented to a robot long-range operation task and comprises the following steps: firstly, taking a pre-trained vision-language-action model as a reference strategy, introducing a residual reinforcement learning expert on the basis of action output of the reference strategy, carrying out hot start through departure strategy data generated by reference strategy roolout, and carrying out reinforcement learning training in combination with in-process strategy data generated by online interaction; the method comprises the following steps of: firstly, acquiring an atomic skill data set, further acquiring error recovery, failure correction, boundary state processing and strategy induction data to form an enhanced skill data set, then performing symbolic modeling on the atomic skill, and establishing a mapping relation between a symbolic action and an atomic skill strategy and a mapping relation between a symbolic parameter and a continuous control parameter; and generating or updating the planning field description file. In the task execution stage, multi-modal input of voice/text instructions, visual perception information, environment states, robot states and the like is obtained, and residual reinforcement learning experts, short board data distillation, training after reinforcement, skill symbolization planning and a double closed-loop error correction mechanism are integrally designed; and the success rate, robustness, expandability and interpretability of long-range operation tasks of the robot are improved.

sources.title: Intelligent chassis reconstruction control method for actuator fault and degradation scene [CN122481785A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an intelligent chassis reconstruction control method for actuator faults and degradation scenes. According to the method, environment images, navigation semantics, vehicle states and executor health state information are obtained in real time, the health state of each chassis executor is evaluated, capability marks are generated, the capability marks are subjected to multi-mode fusion with the environment semantics and the vehicle states after capability coding, and a vision-language-action model is input for reasoning a degraded driving strategy and reconstructing a control intention. And generating a chassis control target according to the intention, and dynamically adjusting the weights of the actuators in combination with an available actuator set and a control distribution strategy to realize control reconstruction. The system further updates the performer capability description and reconstruction strategy based on the vehicle response feedback to improve vehicle stability, safety, and task continuation capability in the event of performer failure, degradation, or response hysteresis.

sources.title: Vision-language-action moving operation method and system based on multi-view geometric vision coding [CN122493520A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vision-language-action moving operation method and system based on multi-view geometric vision coding, and belongs to the field of robot perception control and intelligent ownership. A multi-view geometric vision coder is introduced on the basis of a semantic vision coder of a base vision-language-action model; in combination with residual projection and a low-rank adaptation mode, moving operation training data including multi-view image observation, a language instruction and an expert action sequence are utilized, parameters of a residual projection module, a vision-language model and an attention layer in an action expert are subjected to efficient parameter fine adjustment, fused features can stably participate in action generation, and the action generation efficiency is improved. Therefore, the understanding ability of the model for the target position, the operation area and the three-dimensional space relation is improved, the training cost is reduced, the success rate of continuous tasks of mobile operation such as navigation, approaching, grabbing and putting is improved, and the method is suitable for mobile operation tasks needing spatial reasoning and real robot deployment scenes.

sources.title: Task adaptation training method and control method of vision-language-action model [CN122454312A]
authors: BEIJING YUANLI LINGJI INTELLIGENT TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING YUANLI LINGJI INTELLIGENT TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of computers, and provides a task adaptation training method and control method of a vision-language-action model, a pre-trained VLA model at least comprises a vision language module and an action expert, and the action expert comprises a prior branch with parameters in a frozen state and an adaptation branch with parameters in a trainable state. Wherein in the task adaptation training method, through a differentiated updating strategy, when a downstream task is adapted, the general scene understanding ability contained in a visual language module and the general motion priori contained in a motion expert of a pre-training model are reserved, only adaptation branches are trained, and efficient fine adjustment of parameters is achieved; the risk of over-fitting small-scale downstream data is reduced, and the generalization and robustness of the VLA model under the conditions of out-of-distribution scenes and few samples are improved.

sources.title: Ammeter replacement robot control method based on vision-language-action model [CN122378715A]
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of power equipment operation and maintenance automation and intelligent robots with bodies, and particularly relates to an electricity meter replacement robot control method based on a vision-language-action model. The method comprises the following steps: carrying out input layer and output layer adaptation on a universal vision-language-action model; according to the action feature expression, the current task stage and the mechanical arm state, an action sequence corresponding to box opening, meter disassembling, meter assembling and resetting is generated, and after action parameters in the action sequence are subjected to security constraint verification, the action sequence is sent to a target electric meter replacement robot to be executed; and collecting an actual execution state, and re-inputting the actual execution state as a part of input at the next moment into the vision-language-action model so as to form a closed-loop control process of perception-understanding-action-re-perception. According to the method, the environment adaptability, the operation continuity and the execution safety of the electric meter replacement robot in a complex electric power operation scene can be improved.

sources.title: Vehicle-road dual-channel cooperative driving method oriented to vision-language-action model [CN122368955A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vehicle-road dual-channel cooperative driving method oriented to a vision-language-action model. The method comprises the following steps: in an Internet of Vehicles cooperative perception scene, dividing an image frame extracted by a vehicle at a t moment into a plurality of patches; synchronously calculating the own vehicle and collaborative attention weight of each patch for fusion; dividing the fused attention weight into discrete semantic importance levels according to a quantization threshold value; and matching corresponding control parameters from the compression operator set to execute feature compression processing. Then entering a reinforcement learning agent to output an instruction of main and standby channel allocation action; the main channel is called to send the compression characteristics of all patches, and the standby channel is used for carrying out redundant transmission on the patches of the key semantics; the receiving end counts each index and feeds back; and the own vehicle continues to extract the image frame at the t + 1 moment, the steps are repeated, and after compression features are obtained, the optimized reinforcement learning agent is used for sending the main channel and the standby channel. According to the method, the transmission stability, the real-time performance and efficient utilization of communication resources are remarkably improved.

sources.title: Control method, system and equipment for driving intelligent chassis by passenger personalized preference based on vision-language-action model and storage medium [CN122275950A]
authors: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a control method, system and equipment for driving an intelligent chassis by passenger personalized preference based on a vision-language-action model, and a storage medium, and belongs to the technical field of intelligent automobile control and intelligent chassis cooperative control. The method comprises the following steps: collecting multi-source information; a passenger personalized dynamic experience preference portrait is constructed; scene-preference multi-mode joint modeling is carried out, and unified scene-preference semantic representation is formed; inputting a vision-language-action model to generate a personalized chassis style intention; generating a dynamic performance constraint and a controller parameter adjustment target; generating a specific chassis control target; multi-actuator personalized cooperative control is executed; and performing parameter recovery and preference learning updating. According to the method, visual-language-action joint reasoning among passenger personalized preference, visual scene semantics and chassis control actions is realized, and the comprehensive performance of an automatic driving and auxiliary driving vehicle in the aspects of comfort, stability, safety and personalized experience is improved.

sources.title: Well mining automatic driving method and system based on vision-language-action model [CN122261123A]
authors: CHANGZHOU RESEARCH INST CO LTD OF CHINA COAL TECHNOLOGY AND ENGINEERING GROUP
sources.organization: TIANDI CHANGZHOU AUTOMATION CO, CHANGZHOU RESEARCH INST CO LTD OF CHINA COAL TECHNOLOGY AND ENGINEERING GROUP
sources.abstract: The invention relates to a well mine automatic driving method and system based on a vision-language-action model in the technical field of mine unmanned driving and artificial intelligence, and the method comprises the steps: S1, visual input: collecting images in different directions and synchronous in time through a camera of a vehicle; s2, text input: generating a navigation instruction text through a vehicle GIS map and UWB positioning, or receiving a human navigation command and a self-vehicle historical navigation command; and S3, outputting a definition, fusing visual input and text input results, generating a VLM model, and outputting a future planning trajectory. According to the method, module splitting of a traditional'perception-prediction-planning 'assembly line can be reduced, planning is decomposed into scene understanding, key target, intention, decision making and track five steps, driving logic is explicitly aligned, the model is more stable, controllable and easy to evaluate under complex interaction scenes such as a parking entrance, meeting way giving, gate machine waiting and the like, and the method is suitable for large-scale popularization and application. And decoupling of a map side strategy and model reasoning is realized.

sources.title: Precise aeronautical part assembly method based on multi-modal fusion perception and action generation [CN122263307A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an aeronautical part precise assembly method based on multi-modal fusion perception and action generation, which takes a vision-language-action model (VLA) as a core, and comprises the following steps of: firstly, acquiring a two-dimensional image, a three-dimensional point cloud, force/touch signal multi-modal information and a natural language task instruction of aeronautical part assembly; the method comprises the following steps: firstly, acquiring a multi-modal token, then respectively encoding the multi-modal token to generate a visual token, a state token and a text token, carrying out joint modeling on the multi-modal token through a VLA model to obtain a fusion representation, generating a continuous assembly action sequence including grabbing, moving and aligning based on the representation, and finally decoding the action sequence into a control instruction to drive an execution mechanism to complete precise assembly. According to the method, end-to-end automatic control from environment perception, task understanding to action generation is achieved, the automation level, execution precision and task adaptability of aviation assembly are improved, manual teaching and debugging cost is reduced, and the method is suitable for high-precision automatic assembly scenes of aeronautical parts.

sources.title: Robust vision-language-action model post-training method based on reinforcement learning [CN122200228A]
sources.abstract: A robust vision-language-action model post-training method based on reinforcement learning adopts a'award optimization-data generation-strategy optimization 'end-to-end architecture, and comprises the following steps: firstly, constructing a multi-stage task-oriented award mechanism containing a basic task award, a process optimization award and a constraint penalty term; a task completion state, an execution process and dangerous and invalid behaviors are respectively rewarded and punished according to the principles of modal cooperative constraint, process-result dual limitation and robustness guidance; self-adaptive expert demonstration examples are automatically generated through dynamic environment disturbance and trajectory variation strategies, diversified scenes are simulated, and a multivariate action sequence is generated; and finally, VLA model post-training is completed through two rounds of reinforcement learning training, a demonstration instance is generated in the first round of training, and model parameters are optimized based on the instance in the second round. According to the method, the environment adaptation capability, the operation robustness and the task execution success rate of the VLA model are effectively improved, the collision rate is reduced, and the method is suitable for efficient deployment of the VLA model in industrial operation and other scenes.

sources.title: Vision-language-action model optimization method based on feasible action neighborhood prior [CN122153840A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vision-language-action model optimization method based on feasible action neighborhood priori. The method comprises the steps that operation track data containing a natural language instruction, visual observation and a continuous control action sequence are collected and preprocessed; an autoregression structure of an image encoder, a language encoder and an action decoder is adopted, and a continuous action space is discretized through multi-dimensional binning; defining a feasible action neighborhood based on a value function constraint, modeling the neighborhood by using Gaussian distribution, and introducing a KL divergence regular term and negative logarithm likelihood loss to construct a supervision fine tuning framework; the action distribution width is adaptively adjusted through the AdaFAN algorithm, and the FAN-PPO algorithm introduces geometric constraints in a near-end strategy optimization framework to reduce invalid exploration; and deploying the model to realize closed-loop control. The method is compatible with a mainstream VLA model and hardware, the adaptability and training stability of the model to accumulated visual observation disturbance are remarkably enhanced, and the method is suitable for various robot operation scenes such as industrial flexible manufacturing and family service.

sources.title: Vision-language-action model training method based on stage reasoning and stage optimization [CN122154935A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vision-language-action model training method based on stage reasoning and stage optimization. The method is characterized by comprising the steps of dividing a track and marking stage description, generating stage description and stage progress by utilizing self-attention mechanism autoregression, generating an action sequence and a completion signal through an action generation network of an action head and a completion detection head, constructing human stage preference data, and performing stage preference optimization on a model in an offline state. And performing near-end strategy optimization by using the action reward set by the stage progress. Compared with the prior art, the method has the advantages that a stage action sequence of a long-range task can be understood and generated more finely, the problems that in an existing method, credit distribution granularity is too coarse, preference information is fuzzy, and a model and optimization are not coordinated in stage optimization are well solved, the strategy is continuously adjusted through stage reasoning and stage optimization, and the method is more efficient and reliable. The task completion success rate, efficiency and safety are improved, and the method is universal, simple, convenient and remarkable in effect and has good application prospects.

sources.title: METHOD FOR CONTROLLING ROBOT ON BASIS OF SIMPLIFIED MAPS AND NATURAL LANGUAGE COMMANDS, AND COMPUTER PROGRAM [WO2026116947A1]
sources.abstract: A robot control method for controlling a robot on the basis of simplified maps and natural language commands according to an embodiment of the present invention may comprise the steps of: acquiring an image regarding a space; acquiring a simplified map of the space including the robot's current location and location to be reached, at least some elements depicting the space being omitted from the simplified map; acquiring a command expressed in a natural language, which is to be observed by the robot during operations; generating an input token on the basis of at least one of the image, the simplified map, and the command; and generating a waypoint token by processing the input token with a trained vision-language-action model.

sources.title: Robot grabbing method and system for enhancing model by introducing dynamic space relation graph [CN122125675A]
sources.abstract: The invention provides a robot grabbing method and system for introducing a dynamic space relation graph to enhance a model, and belongs to the technical field of robots, and the method comprises the steps: determining the point cloud data of each object and the geometric attribute data of each object in a current grabbing scene according to a color image of the current grabbing scene and the point cloud data of the current grabbing scene; constructing a dynamic space relation graph based on the point cloud data of each object and the geometric attribute data of each object; generating a structured text prompt based on the dynamic space relation graph and the capture priority score of each object in the dynamic space relation graph; inputting the color image of the current capture scene, the input language instruction and the structured text prompt into a vision-language-action model to obtain a capture pose output by the vision-language-action model; and the mechanical arm is driven to execute grabbing according to the grabbing posture. And through construction of the dynamic space relation graph, the grabbing pose suitable for the scene can be speculated, and then the success probability of robot grabbing is increased.

sources.title: METHOD OF CONTROLLING ROBOT BASED ON SIMPLIFIED MAP AND NATURAL-LANGUAGE COMMAND AND COMPUTER PROGRAM THEREFOR [US20260147350A1]
sources.abstract: An embodiment of the present disclosure provides a method of controlling a robot based on a simplified map and a natural-language command. The method may include acquiring an image of a space, acquiring a simplified map of the space, the simplified map including a current position of a robot and a destination position of the robot and not including at least some elements describing the space, acquiring a natural-language command specifying compliance requirements that the robot is to comply with during an operation of the robot, generating input tokens based on at least one of the image, the simplified map, and the natural-language command, and generating waypoint tokens by processing the input tokens with a trained vision-language-action model.

sources.title: Intelligent chassis unified control method, system and equipment based on vision-language-action model and dynamic feasible region projection and storage medium [CN122058956A]
authors: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses an intelligent chassis unified control method, system and device based on a vision-language-action model and dynamic feasible region projection and a storage medium, and belongs to the technical field of automatic driving and vehicle intelligent control. The method comprises the steps of S1, scene and chassis state acquisition; s2, unified semantic representation generation; s3, outputting high-level chassis behavior semantics; s4, generating an intermediate action description; s5, generating a dynamic feasible region; s6, correcting the reference projection of the target chassis; s7, unified control and control distribution; and S8, outputting cooperation and closed-loop updating. According to the method, an intermediate action description and dynamic feasible region projection mechanism is introduced between the VLA high-level semantic decision and the intelligent chassis low-level control, so that the control implementability, safety, stability, interpretability and multi-actuator cooperative control capability of the automatic driving vehicle in a complex scene are improved.

sources.title: Vision-language-action model-based complex road semantic event-driven intelligent chassis pre-adjustment control method, system and equipment and storage medium [CN122058957A]
authors: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: RUIXING INTELLIGENT YANCHENG TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a vision-language-action model-based complex road semantic event-driven intelligent chassis pre-adjustment control method, system and device and a storage medium, and belongs to the technical field of automatic driving vehicle control and intelligent chassis cooperative control. The method comprises the following steps: acquiring vehicle-related information; performing multi-modal fusion coding on the information obtained in the step S1; generating a chassis pre-adjusting intention; a dynamic advance model is constructed, and whether chassis pre-adjustment is triggered or not is judged; after chassis pre-adjustment is triggered, a chassis pre-adjustment target is generated; executing chassis parameter presetting, mode pre-switching and actuator pre-loading; the chassis control process enters an event period active control stage; and the chassis control process enters a recovery and strategy updating stage. According to the method, vision-language-action driven semantic reasoning and chassis active pre-adjustment of a complex road semantic event are realized, and the comfort, the handling stability and the safety of an automatic driving vehicle in a complex road environment are improved.
